core1b.fresh_task: A white beam crosses a glass prism in air and produces a spectrum. Explain why colors separate and predict what turning the prism upside down does.
core1b.protected_work: Explain color separation and why reversing prism orientation reverses deviation sense.

stages.attempt: A white beam crosses a glass prism in air and produces a spectrum. Explain why colors separate and predict what turning the prism upside down does.
stages.reconstruct: n depends on wavelength; under normal dispersion shorter violet wavelengths have greater deviation toward base. Inverting prism reverses base direction and spatial ordering, not material dispersion.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved answer demonstrates this error: Thinking prism creates colors absent from monochromatic input. Otherwise record insufficient evidence; compare your actual reasoning with the reconstruction.
stages.repair: Separate wavelength composition from wavelength-dependent deviation.
stages.boundary_test: If the refractive index were independent of wavelength, what would white-light output look like?

core1b.fresh_task: For an upright triangular prism in air with horizontal base, draw an incident beam from left, two face normals and a qualitatively correct emerging ray for red and violet under normal dispersion.
